turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in. Sit. What brings you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, this cough is bothering me too much. Dry cough, no phlegm, and I keep fearing something is wrong.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many weeks?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, three weeks... no, actually it is five weeks. I told myself it was only a cold, so I delayed coming.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, doctor. But kindly tell me, is five weeks too long for a cold? At the office I cannot concentrate, and that itself is making me more anxious.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any sputum, chest pain, or breathlessness?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none of those. It is dry only. At night it gets worse and my sleep becomes broken. Is poor sleep dangerous?
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): No. Blood pressure treatment?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, ongoing since last year. Amlodipine five milligrams every morning. They added a second tablet recently, and I am worried that one is the cause.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which tablet, what strength, started when?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Ramipril, two point five milligrams... ah, no, the strip says five milligrams, once at night. I started it about three weeks back.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Swelling of lips or face? Any rash?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No swelling, no rash. My sister is on lisinopril for her pressure, and she warned me these tablets cause cough. I almost stopped mine yesterday. Was that foolish?
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do not stop medicines on your own, and do not copy your sister. I am not putting a firm diagnosis on this cough. It may be the ramipril, or just the tail of that cold.

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): If it may only be a cold, why touch the tablet? And if I stop ramipril, my pressure will shoot up, no? Yesterday at home it was one fifty over ninety... no, wait, I am mixing it up, it was one forty-six over eighty-eight.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Today it is 152 over 94, pulse 78. Lungs are clear, no wheeze.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): 152? That is quite high, doctor. Do I need admission? Please, I need a straight answer, my mind is running.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): No admission. Stop ramipril from tonight. I will start telmisartan forty milligrams once in the morning, with the amlodipine.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Telmisartan, is it safe? I am fifty-four only. How many days for the cough to go? I read about TB online and now I cannot get that thought out.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not labelling this as TB today. The cough can linger a few weeks after the tablet is stopped. Continue amlodipine five milligrams every morning.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): You still sound unsure about the cause. So why are we changing the medicine if you are not sure? I need to understand, otherwise I will worry all week.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your pressure is above target, and the ramipril might be contributing. We switch and watch. That is enough for today.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, okay. Any blood test? My cousin did a scan for cough and they found a spot. Should I also do a scan now? I am quite scared, doctor.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): No blood test today. We might do a chest scan if it does not settle. Let's see in two weeks.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks? What if it becomes worse before that? The medical shop near my house will give cough syrup without a note. Can I take it?
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the cough worsens, or you get breathlessness or swelling of the face, come the same day. No cough syrup unless I prescribe it. Do not take your sister's lisinopril.

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I won't take her tablets, promise. Honey in warm water I have been taking, is that allowed? And I walk every morning by the lake. Should I stop walking till this settles?
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Honey water is fine. Keep walking if you are comfortable. Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor, no allergy that I know of. What if telmisartan also brings the cough? Then what will you give? Sorry, I am asking too many questions.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Different group. It does not typically cause this cough. Take it every morning, no skipping. Check BP at home twice a week and note the readings.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Morning or night for the checking? And is forty milligrams a big dose to start? There is a health camp at my office next month. Should I wait and show them?
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning readings are enough. Forty milligrams is a usual starting dose. Do not wait for the camp.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Also, because of this cough my sleep is very broken. Just for a few days, can I have a sleeping tablet? I have a presentation on Thursday and I need to be fresh.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): No sleeping tablet. Deal with the cough. You will manage the presentation.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): The waiting was so long today I nearly went home, and the fan outside is not even working. Sorry, that is beside the point.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fine. Repeat the plan once.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Tonight I skip ramipril, telmisartan from tomorrow morning, amlodipine as usual, and I see you in two weeks. If the cough stays you might scan. Correct?
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Correct. No ramipril tonight. Telmisartan starts tomorrow morning. Reception will book the two-week visit.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): If the cough goes in a few days, do I still come? And should I bring the home BP notes?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Still come in two weeks. Yes, bring the notes.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister wanted me to ask if she should stop lisinopril also. She coughs in the winter sometimes.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not her doctor. She needs her own visit. You follow only your plan.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. I will stop ramipril tonight and start the new tablet tomorrow, and I will try not to panic.
